## Problem

The lab posture `mlflow-lab-target` declares is for lab VMs on an
isolated segment. The hardened posture asks a specific question: can
the SAME server run with `labReachable = false` and a loopback
`host`, fronted by a reverse proxy for the real deployment, and can
you SHOW the flip moved the surface (every probe that succeeded
against the lab posture re-run and now refused)?

## Solution

Tighten the posture in the configuration, front it, and re-probe with
the SAME instrument (`../attack-defence/attack-then-verify.html`'s
probe pair):

```nix
# configuration.nix — the hardened posture
services.kailash.mlflow.labReachable = false;   # back to the default
# and an explicit loopback bind; NOTE: labReachable and host are
# mutually exclusive options (the module asserts this at eval),
services.kailash.mlflow.host = "127.0.0.1";     # so set only this
services.kailash.mlflow.openFirewall = false;   # stays false — see below

# the proxy is YOURS to declare (the module ships no auth option):
services.nginx.enable = true;
# nginx site: proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; + your TLS + authn
```

Re-probe with the same instrument, same seed — the pair recipe's
stages MUST refuse when pointed at the hardened posture:

```bash
# same seed, same probes, posture flipped (see attack-then-verify):
kailash-integration-mlflow-attack --seed
# -> ATTEMPTED/FAIL verdicts: the hardened bind closes the surface
#    the unauthenticated tracking + artefact probes now show FAIL
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
== KA-23 integration-mlflow-attack acceptance pair ==
tracking : http://127.0.0.1:5000
track: ATTEMPTED — POST /api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search (UNAUTH)
track: FAIL — surface closed (auth/bind now gate it)
bypass(seed): ATTEMPTED — ...
bypass(seed): FAIL — surface closed
mlflow-attack: seed verdict = FAIL (expected FAIL under hardened posture)
```

## Discussion

- **The no-auth fact, explicitly:** the kailash mlflow service
  module at the pin ships NO first-class auth option (no
  `auth.enable`, no basic-auth token, no service account). The
  intended production posture is therefore
  **reverse-proxy-with-auth on your side** — nginx/Envoy/what-you-declare
  in front of 127.0.0.1:5000. If a future module pin adds auth
  options, re-read the module and re-write this recipe in the same
  change.
- **The option truth table at the pin:**

  | Option (at pin) | Lab posture | Hardened posture |
  |---|---|---|
  | `labReachable` | `true` → `0.0.0.0:5000` | `false` (default; loopback) |
  | `host` | (unset; labReachable instead) | `"127.0.0.1"` explicit |
  | `openFirewall` | `false` | `false` — stays false |
  | auth | none offered | reverse proxy (your config) |

- **Why `openFirewall` stays `false` in both postures:** the module
  defaults `openFirewall = false` and the hardened posture must not
  undo that — loopback bind + proxy is the design; a firewall hole
  would defeat the point of the bind. Treat any future
  firewall-open change as a red flag in review, not a convenience.
- **Same-seed re-probe FAIL pattern:** the lab→hardened flip is the
  same instrument with posture options reversed; the expected
  verdict moves from `ok` to `FAIL` for the pair's two
  probes. Compare with the pair recipe's acceptance record:
  `ok` under lab posture, `FAIL` under hardened — a config diff,
  not a code diff, is what moved the verdicts. If hardened probes
  still show `ok`, the flip did not land; do NOT write that up as
  success.
- **The upstream caveat still applies:** the mlflow server's own
  `--host` warning ("NOT a security setting") is why the hardened
  posture is BIND + PROXY, not "rely on defaults". Loopback is the
  transport boundary; the proxy's auth is the API boundary; both are
  needed before the tracking API can be called production.
